text.title: RAG Policy Thresholds Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete `RAGPolicy` for a checkout project with four signals, a logged override in week 20 and a Red fired in week 21, with a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad policy showing what the validator prints and what the sponsor sees beyond it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: The checkout project reports weekly to a sponsor. In Q4 2025 the same team lost the Acme account after a 30% schedule overrun that had been reported Green for six weeks; the PMO tolerance policy now sets schedule tolerance at 10% / 20%. In Q1 2026 a hotfix incident escaped to production without any signal turning Amber. The PM (olena.k) reviews the policy on 2026-05-10, computes week 20 on 2026-05-18 and week 21 on 2026-05-25.

example.title: checkout RAGPolicy 1.4.0, reviewed 2026-05-10, two cycles computed
example.code: { "project_id": "checkout", "header": { "owner": {"role": "pm", "person": "olena.k"}, "version": "1.4.0", "last_reviewed": "2026-05-10", "reporting_cadence_days": 7 }, "signals": [ { "signal_id": "schedule_variance_pct", "unit": "percent", "input_source": {"system": "Jira", "query": "dashboard 'Checkout EV' panel 'SV%' = (EV - PV) / PV * 100"}, "comparator": "gt", "amber_threshold": 10, "red_threshold": 20, "evidence": ["incident-2025-Q4-acme-overrun", "policy://pmo/schedule-tolerance"] }, { "signal_id": "budget_variance_pct", "unit": "percent", "input_source": {"system": "NetSuite", "query": "saved export 'checkout-cost-vs-plan' column CV%"}, "comparator": "gt", "amber_threshold": 5, "red_threshold": 15, "evidence": ["policy://pmo/budget-tolerance"] }, { "signal_id": "defect_escape_rate", "unit": "ratio", "input_source": {"system": "Sentry", "query": "saved search 'checkout prod new issues / releases' weekly"}, "comparator": "gt", "amber_threshold": 0.05, "red_threshold": 0.1, "evidence": ["postmortem-2026-Q1-checkout-hotfix"] }, { "signal_id": "blockers_open_count", "unit": "count", "input_source": {"system": "Jira", "query": "project = CHK AND flagged = Impediment AND status != Done"}, "comparator": "gte", "amber_threshold": 2, "red_threshold": 4, "evidence": ["baseline-chk-2026-q1-blockers"] } ], "actions": { "green": "continue the weekly cadence; record value, version and last_reviewed", "amber": {"step": "PM runs a mid-week health check with the tech lead and posts findings in the status thread", "deadline_hours": 72}, "red": {"playbook": "distressed-project-rescue", "first_step": "sponsor notified and rescue playbook opened", "within_hours": 4, "fires_at": "compute_time"} }, "review_log": [ { "logged_at": "2026-05-10", "kind": "review", "person": "olena.k", "version_after": "1.4.0", "signals_removed": [{"signal_id": "pr_review_latency_hours", "reason": "no Amber or Red in Q4 2025 and Q1 2026"}], "signals_justified": [{"signal_id": "budget_variance_pct", "reason": "no Amber in two periods but it is the sponsor's contractual tolerance"}], "signals_added_or_tightened": [{"signal_id": "defect_escape_rate", "reason": "Q1 hotfix incident was not flagged ahead; amber tightened from 0.08 to 0.05", "evidence": ["postmortem-2026-Q1-checkout-hotfix"]}] }, { "logged_at": "2026-05-18", "kind": "override", "person": "olena.k", "cycle_date": "2026-05-18", "computed_colour": "amber", "reported_colour": "green", "reason": "Jira EV panel double-counted the sprint 14 carry-over; corrected SV% is 6" } ], "colour_history": [ { "computed_at": "2026-05-18", "policy_version": "1.4.0", "policy_last_reviewed": "2026-05-10", "values": [ {"signal_id": "schedule_variance_pct", "value": 12}, {"signal_id": "budget_variance_pct", "value": 3}, {"signal_id": "defect_escape_rate", "value": 0.02}, {"signal_id": "blockers_open_count", "value": 1} ], "computed_colour": "amber", "reported_colour": "green" }, { "computed_at": "2026-05-25", "policy_version": "1.4.0", "policy_last_reviewed": "2026-05-10", "values": [ {"signal_id": "schedule_variance_pct", "value": 22}, {"signal_id": "budget_variance_pct", "value": 4}, {"signal_id": "defect_escape_rate", "value": 0.03}, {"signal_id": "blockers_open_count", "value": 1} ], "computed_colour": "red", "reported_colour": "red", "red_escalated_at": "2026-05-25T10:40" } ] }
example.note: Every threshold is a number in the unit the query returns: percent for the two earned-value variances, a ratio for defect escapes, a count for blockers. There is no "significant" anywhere (r-threshold-numeric-with-comparator).
All four signals use `gt` / `gte`, so red is the larger number on each; a coverage-style `lt` signal would carry the smaller number as red (r-red-strictly-beyond-amber).

`schedule_variance_pct` and `budget_variance_pct` are percent variances against plan, not "3 days late" or "12k over"; each `input_source` names the system and the panel, export or JQL a second person can run (r-input-source-is-a-query).

The 10 / 20 schedule thresholds are anchored to the Acme overrun and the PMO tolerance policy; the 0.05 defect line to the Q1 hotfix post-mortem; the blocker line to the Q1 baseline. Each is something the PM can point at when asked to loosen it (r-evidence-anchor-per-signal).

Week 20: SV% = 12 is over Amber (10), everything else is Green, so `computed_colour` is amber; it was reported green only because a logged override names the data glitch, the corrected value and the person (r-worst-signal-wins, r-override-logged-never-downgrades-red).

Week 21: SV% = 22 is over Red (20). Budget, defects and blockers are all Green and the colour is still red; `red_escalated_at` is 10:40 on the compute day, inside the 4-hour bound, and no override could have reported it lower (r-worst-signal-wins, r-red-action-named-and-time-bound).
The Amber deadline is 72 hours, inside the 168-hour weekly cycle; the Red action names the playbook, the first step, the bound and `compute_time` (r-red-action-named-and-time-bound).

The 2026-05-10 review removed a signal that never fired in two periods, justified one that did not fire but is contractual, and tightened the defect signal with the post-mortem as its new anchor; both cycles cite version 1.4.0 and a `policy_last_reviewed` 8 and 15 days earlier (r-review-within-90-days-prunes-and-adds).

example.title: What the validator and the sponsor reject
example.note: Validator output: `$.signals[0].input_source.query: matches forbidden 'not' schema`, `$.signals[0].amber_threshold: expected number, got str`, `$.signals[0].evidence[0]: 'TBD' does not match pattern '^(incident-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+|postmortem-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+|policy://[^\s]+|baseline-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)$'`, `$.actions.amber.step: matches forbidden 'not' schema`, `$.actions.red.fires_at: must equal 'compute_time', got 'next_sync'`, `$.review_log[0].reported_colour: must equal 'red', got 'amber'`.

Once those are fixed, the cross-field block reports: `signals[test_coverage_pct]: red_threshold 70 must be less than amber_threshold 60 for lt (r-red-strictly-beyond-amber)` and `colour_history[0]: computed_colour 'amber' but the worst signal is 'red'; no averaging (r-worst-signal-wins)`.

What the sponsor sees beyond the validator: a schedule number that is whatever the PM said on Monday, a coverage signal that can never be Amber (below 70 is already Red, so 60 is unreachable as a warning), and a week in which SV% = 22 crossed the Red line the policy itself set and the report said Amber because the steering committee was on Thursday. That is the Acme run of Green reports again, with a policy on file.
